key_insight: Nonlinear surface acoustic waves can generate dislocations, restructure surfaces, and drive nonthermal defect annealing in platinum.
engineering_relevance: Acoustic processing could enable control of near-surface defects and atomic-scale roughness, with potential relevance to platinum catalysis.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of nonlinear Rayleigh waves in platinum.
Comparison of wave evolution on Pt(111) and Pt(001).
Tracking of dislocation reactions, surface restructuring, and repeated-wave annealing.
evidence_signal: Simulations show rapid shock formation on Pt(111), weaker sharpening on Pt(001), and progressive dislocation-density reduction with repeated wave passages.
watch_item: Experimental validation is needed to establish practical wave amplitudes and whether the simulated surface changes enhance catalytic activity.
paper_title: Generation and non-thermal annealing of dislocations and atomic-scale roughness by nonlinear surface acoustic waves
